data.description:
## Goal

Make the `/slots` single-flight helper in `proxy/proxy/observability.py`
cancellation-safe: a leader that is cancelled (browser disconnect cancels the SSE
handler) must never orphan the shared future, and a follower must never `await`
that future without a bound. This is the core fix for parent
LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y (AC1, AC2, AC3, AC5).

## Current defect (verified)

```python
if not leader:
    return await fut                     # unbounded follower wait
except Exception as exc:                 # CancelledError is BaseException
    if not fut.done():
        fut.set_exception(exc)
    raise
finally:
    async with lock:
        _slots_poll_inflight.pop(url, None)   # owner forgotten, future PENDING
```

`asyncio.CancelledError` bypasses `except Exception`, so the future is left
pending forever while the registry entry is removed — every follower hangs, and
`_periodic_broadcast_loop()` can stall for all connected clients.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: A follower awaiting an in-flight `/slots` fetch is released when the leader is cancelled (`asyncio.CancelledError`), rather than blocking forever; `_fetch_slots_payload()` resolves or cancels the shared future on that (or any `BaseException`) before re-raising, and the regression test from LP-0MVK1YCVV007HNAG passes.
- AC2: A follower never waits unboundedly — if the leader disappears without resolving the future, the follower either re-fetches as a new leader (re-registering the inflight future) or returns the last-known/cached values within its own timeout; the wait must not cancel the shared future for other followers (`asyncio.shield` / `asyncio.wait`, not a bare `wait_for(fut)`).
- AC3: Cancelling a request that owns the single-flight fetch does not leak a pending future or emit "Future exception was never retrieved" / "Task was destroyed but it is pending" warnings; LP-0MVK1YCVV007HNAG AC3 passes.
- AC4: The documented reproduction fails before the fix and passes after it, using the existing test-skill runner (no ad-hoc pytest invocations); the before/after output and the changed-scope suite result are recorded in a comment on this item.
- AC5: `_periodic_broadcast_loop()`'s follower path can no longer stall permanently — verified by trace/reasoning plus the coalescer-level tests (no new loop-level test is required).

## Approach (smallest end-to-end slice)

- Replace `except Exception` with `except BaseException` (or
  `except (Exception, asyncio.CancelledError)`) and resolve the future before
  re-raising: `if not fut.done(): fut.cancel()` is acceptable, but prefer
  setting a defensive result so followers degrade to last-known values rather
  than raising.
- Bound the follower path with the caller's own `timeout` (or a dedicated
  `SLOTS_POLL_FOLLOWER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`, default ≤ `timeout`) using
  `asyncio.shield`, then fall back to a fresh leader attempt / cached payload.
- Keep the `finally` cleanup: registry entry removed only when this caller still
  owns it (avoid popping a newer leader's future).
- Add a short comment block documenting the invariant (future always resolved;
  follower wait always bounded) and reference LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:295` — `_fetch_slots_payload()`: cancellation-safe future handling and bounded follower wait.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:226` — `_slots_poll_inflight` / `_slots_poll_cache` registry semantics.
- `proxy/proxy/observability.py:1737` — `_periodic_broadcast_loop()` follower path (the all-clients stall).
- `proxy/tests/test_slots_poll_coalescing.py` — regression tests that must pass after the fix.
data.title: Resolve orphaned single-flight future on leader cancellation

data.description:
## Goal

Bound `proxy.ui.status_events()`'s initial payload assembly so the SSE stream
always emits a first frame — real status payload or `: keepalive` — within a
bounded time, even when `query_llama_status()` (or the other initial queries) is
slow or degraded. This closes AC4 of parent LP-0MVJML600003CQ6Y.

## Current defect (verified)

`status_events()`'s `event_generator()` awaits `srv.query_llama_status()`
unbounded, then `router_list_models()`, `_get_per_model_queries()` and the 5 s
`_query_slots_detail()` — all **before** the `while` loop that emits the 30 s
keepalive. A stalled backend therefore yields zero bytes forever; the TCP
connection stays up, so the browser `EventSource` never reconnects and the UI
looks frozen.

## Acceptance Criteria

- AC1: `status_events()` emits its initial payload or a keepalive within a bounded time even when `query_llama_status()` is slow or degraded: the initial payload assembly is wrapped in one bounded budget, and on timeout the generator yields a degraded status payload or a `: keepalive` comment instead of blocking, then enters the normal keepalive loop.
- AC2: The regression test from LP-0MVK1YD81004DPYZ passes: first frame within the bound while `query_llama_status()` stalls, plus a second frame within the bound.
- AC3: The happy-path payload is unchanged (same keys, including `slots` and `quota`) when the backend answers promptly — existing `test_slot_sse.py` and `test_quota_observability.py` `status_events` tests still pass.
- AC4: Client disconnects during the bounded initial query still tear the handler down promptly (`srv.sse_clients.discard(queue)` in `finally` runs); no queue leaks from a timed-out initial payload.

## Approach (smallest end-to-end slice)

- Wrap the initial-payload coroutine in `asyncio.wait_for(...)` with a budget
  shorter than the keepalive interval (candidate: 5 s, or reuse the existing
  /slots 5 s detail timeout as the single worst case).
- On `TimeoutError`, yield a minimal degraded status payload (keeping the SSE
  contract: `{"type": "status", ...}`) or `: keepalive`; then continue into the
  existing `while True` keepalive/broadcast loop.
- Do not change the frontend; a missing/stale `slots` block is already tolerated.

## Key Files

- `proxy/proxy/ui.py:347` — `status_events()` / `event_generator()`: bound the initial payload, degrade to keepalive.
- `proxy/tests/test_slot_sse.py` — `status_events` regression tests that must pass.
- `proxy/tests/test_quota_observability.py` — payload-shape assertions that must keep passing.
data.title: Bound status_events initial payload so keepalive always arrives
